difficulty_reason: Prove that for any invertible L on X_K there is an invertible L_0 on X with dim H^0(X_K, L tensor L_0) = 1 and H^1 = 0: after picking an ample L_0 and tensoring with L_0^{tensor n} for n >> 0 (vanishing by coherent-lemma-vanshing-gives-ample, nonvanishing by degree), descend-induct on t = dim H^0; for t > 1 use that the k-rational points are Zariski dense in X_K (varieties-lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense) to pick x with a nonzero section s not vanishing at x_K; the exact sequence 0 -> I tensor L -> L -> i_*i^*L -> 0 with H^0(i_*i^*L) of dimension 1 gives surjectivity of H^0(L) -> H^0(i_*i^*L), hence dim H^0(I tensor L) = t - 1 and H^1(I tensor L) = 0 from the long exact sequence.
